messages:
jordan: Customer reported an oddity — daily usage chart in Console shows 0 tokens for 2026-03-12 but their CSV export contains ~42,000 tokens. Org id org_4321. They noticed it when reconciling billing. Screenshot uploaded.
sam: Can you paste the export rows (first/last) and the org timezone? Also which chart — the daily tokens bar chart on Billing > Usage?
jordan: Yes the Billing > Usage daily chart. Org timezone in account settings is set to Pacific/Chatham (UTC+12:45). Export first/last rows:
```
2026-03-12,42000,token_count
2026-03-13,38000,token_count
```
But Dashboard shows 03-12 as zero, 03-13 has combined 80k.
lee: Weird — very unusual TZ (:+12:45). Our aggregation pipeline uses date_trunc on a UTC-ts converted to org_tz in two places: dashboard rendering path vs exports path. They should match but maybe one path normalizes to IANA tz and another to an offset.
metrics-bot: alert: missing-datapoints org_4321 day-bucket 2026-03-12 detected at 1990123468
jordan: I pulled raw events from usage_events:
```sql
select count(*) as tokens, date_trunc('day', timestamp at time zone 'UTC' at time zone account_tz) as local_day
from usage_events
where org_id = 'org_4321' and timestamp between '2026-03-12' and '2026-03-14'
group by 2;
```
Result: tokens for local_day 2026-03-12 = 42000. So ingestion fine, export fine, dashboard rendering off.
sam: Can you check the frontend request that fetches daily-series? Maybe the API is sending timezone offset instead of IANA name; some of our TZ conversion util drops minute offsets and ends up rounding to nearest hour which would move the day boundary for +12:45.
jordan: Attached browser network trace shows request: GET /api/usage/daily?tz=+12:45&org=org_4321
lee: There's the bug — API expects tz param as IANA name (e.g., Pacific/Chatham) for server-side conversion. If tz is +12:45 we use a different codepath that converts to minutes and then to an offset-timezone name we don't support, falling back to UTC in the renderer. That would zero out the 03-12 bucket and push tokens into 03-13.
lee: I found a log at usage-renderer-2026-03-12-03.log: 
"WARN convert_tz: unrecognized tz offset +12:45 for org org_4321, defaulting to UTC"
sam: Ok that explains behaviour. Any customers with high-minute-offset tzs are affected. Good catch.
jordan: Customer is blocked — asking for ETA and a workaround.
lee: Quick mitigation: force the exporter to pass IANA tz name (we can update frontend to use account_tz string instead of user browser tz). I'll open a hotfix PR to coerce +HH:MM offsets to the matched IANA tz when available, fallback to using account_tz from the account service if present.
lee: PR #3456 opened: fix/dashboard-tz-offset-to-iana. Will run tests and deploy to staging.
metrics-bot: deploy started to staging for PR #3456 at 1990123501
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded to staging in 4m 12s at 1990123543
sam: Sam here — can we do a quick canary on one org (org_4321) in staging and show dashboard now matches export?
lee: Deployed to staging. Jordan can you flip the staging flag and point the customer to temporary staging preview? Or we can run a one-off rerender using account_tz on prod dashboard for that org.
jordan: I ran the staging preview — staging dashboard now shows 42k on 03-12 matching export. Customer confirmed temporarily in the shared call. They're happy with workaround but want prod fix timeline.
lee: Plan: hotfix to prod tonight (low-risk change: tz parsing and fallback), rollback window 60m. I'll add a post-deploy smoke that compares one-day buckets vs export for any orgs with minute-offset timezones.
sam: I'll draft customer-facing note: explain mismatch, provide workaround (use CSV export or staging preview), and give ETA: hotfix tonight (ETC 3 hours).
jordan: Thanks — attaching the PR, logs, and screenshots to the case. Moving to eng-analytics for the prod rollout. :thumbsup:
lee: Adding follow-up ticket ENG-9421 to handle long-term: normalize timezone sources across services + add unit tests for non-hour offsets.
sam: Reaction :eyes: on the ticket.
metrics-bot: scheduled prod deploy for PR #3456 at 1990127200
